routes._comment: Racemic (untagged) oral IR profile at priority 1, the same fix methylphenidate already carries. The resolved community profile spliced drug.community's onset/peak/offset — a source whose onset already absorbs the come-up, so it publishes no comeup row — with psychonautwiki's comeup 30-135, double-counting ~82 min. The cumulated boundaries came to 562 min (9 h 22 m) while the card's own trio printed the same profile's total as '4-8 h': one screen, two answers. That is the 'Adderall IR graph doesn't seem right' report. Phases below sum to ~325 min against a 240-420 min total, so the curve and the stated total agree. Doses are the recreational ladder the majority of upstream sources already publish for racemic oral amphetamine; they must be present because a route with no `doses` still emits an (empty) dose row that would classify every dose as sub-threshold.

combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: Phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, etc. — MAO inhibition removes the main breakdown route for the released norepinephrine and dopamine, so pressor effects stack into hypertensive crisis. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: The stimulant masks how tired and how drunk you are, so both tend to get redosed past where either would go alone. Cardiovascular load adds up; judgment of it does not.

combinations.name: Other stimulants
combinations.description: Cocaine, MDMA, caffeine in quantity — heart rate and blood pressure effects are additive. Stacking stimulants raises the cardiovascular load faster than it raises the effect you wanted.

combinations.name: SSRIs
combinations.description: Amphetamine's serotonin release is minor, so the combination is common and mostly uneventful — but reuptake inhibition can accentuate the norepinephrine side: more jitter, higher pulse. Worth noticing, not fearing.

waterHeat.headline: Sip to thirst
waterHeat.body: Stimulants suppress thirst without changing how much fluid you actually need — which isn't much more than usual unless you're dancing or in the heat. Sip to thirst rather than forcing water; a dry mouth is from reduced saliva, not dehydration.
